display.purpose: The product name on the landing's first screen. Uppercase. The table's logo and the front desk's wordmark are the same face at their own sizes.

headline.purpose: One slab headline per landing section.

headline-desk.purpose: The single foil-clipped slab line over the board at /play and at the gate, held to 16ch.

title.purpose: Slab headings on paper and on boards.

title-stub.purpose: The slab title of a stub on the front desk's ticket, in red ink.

amount.purpose: A pot, a stake or a prize on a stub, in red ink, tabular; a balance is 26px.

title-sans.purpose: A sub-heading on the ground that should not compete with the section headline.

lede.purpose: The sentence under a headline, max 62ch.

body.purpose: Prose on the landing; 16px on paper.

body-desk.purpose: The base size of the front desk and the gate.

body-app.purpose: The base size of the game table.

small-paper.purpose: Explanations, fields and pickers on a stub; 600 for a field's label.

fine.purpose: The line under an action on a stub, in Soft Ink.

label.purpose: Status chips and name tags on the landing, uppercase.

label-desk.purpose: The status chip on the front desk's boards, uppercase.

label-board.purpose: Column heads on a board and the small line over a seat's name or a term, uppercase.

data.purpose: Transaction hashes and match ids on boards; system mono stack.

flap.purpose: One character to a split-flap cell, capitals and figures.

shadows.name: ticket-on-ground
shadows.purpose: A filter on the unmasked parent of any masked paper object on the landing, and of the ticket on the front desk; 45% under the itinerary strip.

shadows.name: foil-lettering
shadows.purpose: The shade under foil-clipped slab lettering, on the landing and the front desk.

shadows.name: foil-lettering-hero
shadows.purpose: First-screen name, wordmark and departures heading (lengths scale with the first screen's unit).

shadows.name: go-button
shadows.purpose: Lower edge and short cast of the gold pill on paper, landing and front desk; removed when disabled.

shadows.name: speech-note
shadows.purpose: The agent's cream notes on the landing's ground; 0 4px 12px at the table; none on a front-desk stub.

motion.name: deal
motion.purpose: The itinerary strip arrives once, stub by stub; removed under reduced motion.

motion.name: flap
motion.purpose: A new flap cell drops in from its top edge (from rotateX(-62deg), brightness 1.7). Only cells whose character changed are new. Not run under reduced motion.

motion.name: deal-desk
motion.purpose: The front desk's stubs settle once on arrival (from 16px lower and -0.7deg). Not run under reduced motion.

motion.name: rise
motion.purpose: The board plate on the first screen.

motion.name: lift
motion.purpose: Hover lift of the gold pill (2px, landing and front desk), of a transaction stub (4px), and the 3px slide of a board row's arrow.

motion.name: wash
motion.purpose: Background and border colour changes on rows and segments.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Incumbent, table: buttons scale to 0.97 while pressed.

gradients.name: hall-ground
gradients.purpose: The page ground of the landing and the front desk. On the landing the stop lengths scale with the first screen's unit; on the front desk they are fixed.

gradients.name: table-ground
gradients.purpose: Incumbent: the ground of the game table.

gradients.name: board
gradients.purpose: Departures boards and ledgers, landing and front desk.

gradients.name: go-button
gradients.purpose: The fill of the one gold pill on a ticket.

gradients.name: flap-cell
gradients.purpose: The face of a split-flap cell, with its hinge line.

plates.name: gold-foil
plates.purpose: Clipped to slab lettering on the ground and on boards, landing and front desk; tiled 360 to 520px wide outside the landing's first screen.

plates.name: strip-paper
plates.purpose: Paper grain tiled over Ticket Paper (180px on the landing's stubs, 420px on the fare table, the closing ticket and the front desk's stubs).

narrative.overview:
Deedlords is drawn as an airport for a board game. A match is a flight: it is listed on a departures board, boarded with a ticket, and paid out at landing. Three materials do all the work. A deep red ground, lit from the top centre, holds the prose. Cream ticket paper, cut by perforations and notched at its corners, holds a match's facts and the action that starts one. Near-black boards with a gold hairline hold what is read from the chain: open matches, the seats of one match, transaction ledgers. Gold slab lettering names things; a geometric sans says everything else.

The system is warm and physical, never glassy or technical. The chain is shown as printed matter: a transaction is a stub you can pick up, a ledger is a board you can read down, a status that changes is a row of split-flap cells that turn. Small isometric vignettes of the board's own squares stand in for illustration on the landing. Density is high on paper and boards (tabular figures, short lines) and generous on the ground (one headline, one lede, wide vertical gaps).

The world is built on three surfaces and they are not identical. The landing and the front desk share the same materials: the same ground gradient, Foil Gold, Ticket Paper with its grain plate, the same board. The front desk is the working form of it: the board hangs on the left as a wall, one ticket of stacked stubs lies on the right as a desk, and the paper carries form controls the landing does not have. The game table was not rebuilt: it keeps a lighter, redder ground and a flat gold of its own. The name "The Departures Hall" was chosen by the documenting pass from the built forms and has not been confirmed by the owner.
keyCharacteristics: Three materials: red ground, cream ticket paper, near-black board. Each has one job.
Tickets are divided by dashed perforations and bitten corners, not by gaps or borders.
Gold is lettering and the one primary action of a stub; green is "boarding"; nothing else is an accent.
Alfa Slab One for names, headlines and amounts; Be Vietnam Pro for everything else.
Only paper casts a shadow. Boards and prose sit level and flat.
A status that changes on a board is set in split-flap cells; a board is never short, its empty lines stand blank.
Every figure is set in tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Three Materials Rule
rules.body: On the landing and the front desk every surface is ground, paper or board. Ground carries prose, paper carries a match and its action and whatever belongs to the visitor, boards carry what is read from the chain. The game table was not rebuilt and keeps its own incumbent surfaces.

rules.name: The Two Golds Rule
rules.body: Foil Gold belongs to the landing and the front desk, Flat Gold to the game table. This is recorded as a difference in the build, not as a design decision; do not introduce a third.

rules.name: The Slab Says Little Rule
rules.body: Alfa Slab One sets names, headlines and amounts (the pot, the fare result, a balance, the two initials in the account stamp), and nothing smaller than 19px on the landing or the front desk. It never sets a sentence of body text.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Times, stakes, seat counts, returns and hashes are set with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, so a board's columns hold still as its numbers change.

rules.name: The Level Ground Rule
rules.body: At rest only the landing's tickets tilt: the itinerary strip by -5.08deg (-1.2deg when stacked), the closing ticket by -1.4deg (-1deg), the first stub's button by -3deg. Boards, prose and lists are never tilted, and the front desk's ticket lies level: it is a form to be filled. Motion is not tilt: a stub may settle from -0.7deg as it is dealt, and a flap turns on its top edge as it drops in.

rules.name: The Paper Casts, Boards Sit Rule
rules.body: On the landing and the front desk, shadow means "this is paper". A board gets a 1.5px border of Foil Gold at 55% and a top-to-bottom gradient from `night-top` to `night`, and no shadow.

dos: Do put a match's facts and its one action on Ticket Paper, what is read from the chain on a Night board, and prose directly on the ground.
Do divide a ticket with a 2px dashed perforation and bitten corners; shadow it with `filter: drop-shadow` on the unmasked parent.
Do give a stub one gold pill at most; every other action on paper is an ink outline, solid ink or quiet.
Do spell a status that changes on a board in split-flap cells keyed by character, and keep the green chip for "boarding".
Do dress standard form controls in ink on paper (Field Cream fill, ink border at 30%, `red` accent) rather than drawing new ones.
Do set every time, amount, count and hash in tabular numerals, and make every chain identifier a link to its transaction or account, as the landing does.
Do keep Alfa Slab One at 19px or larger, for names, headlines and amounts only.
Do mark what does not exist yet with a dashed outline: the word Coming, an open seat.
Do draw new illustration as small isometric vignettes of the board's own squares, and keep each raster's generation prompt with the file, as `assets/plates/` does.
Do honour `prefers-reduced-motion`: entrances are removed and transitions shortened, as every stylesheet already does.
donts: Don't clip the gold-foil plate to anything but slab lettering on the dark ground or a board: on paper the same lettering is flat `red`.
Don't tilt a board, a list or a paragraph, or the front desk's ticket; only the landing's tickets tilt at rest.
Don't put a `box-shadow` on masked paper (the mask cuts it off) or a shadow under a board.
Don't set flap cells on paper or on the ground; they belong to boards.
Don't add a third gold or another ground red; the two of each that exist are a recorded difference between the landing and front desk on one side and the game table on the other.
Don't carry the first screen's window-scaled comp units to another screen: below the fold the landing itself returns to fixed and clamped sizes, and the front desk uses none.
Don't use any Monopoly name, art or wording; the corners are Departure, Customs, Transit Lounge and Visa Denied.
